rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Work near overhead power lines must be carefully planned and carried out to avoid accidental contact or dangerous proximity.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Direct contact is not necessary for injury because a close approach can cause a flashover.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Overhead lines found within or adjoining a work area should be assumed live unless their owner proves otherwise.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Line owners or distribution network operators should be consulted before work near overhead conductors.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Eliminating the hazard by avoiding the area, diverting the line or making it dead is preferred where practicable.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Where elimination is not possible, access routes and work zones must be controlled with suitable precautions.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Plant and material movements near overhead lines should be directly supervised by a suitable person.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Long or high equipment such as cranes, MEWPs, scaffold poles, tipper bodies and ladders presents particular risk.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: Overhead-line risk depends on voltage, clearance, equipment dimensions, route, weather, ground conditions, supervision and line-owner controls.

rows.source: HSE overhead-power-line work safety
rows.verified: HSE overhead-line evidence is line-, site-, task-, equipment-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level electrocution probability.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: PUWER requires work equipment to be maintained in an efficient state, in efficient order and in good repair.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Where machinery has a maintenance log, the log must be kept up to date.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Maintenance operations on work equipment must be capable of being carried out safely.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Maintenance should be planned and supported by clear instructions and communication before work starts.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Machinery should be securely isolated where unexpected powered movement could injure people during maintenance.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Manufacturer instructions should guide maintenance, particularly for safety-critical features.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Inspection should identify deterioration before it creates a health and safety risk.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Maintenance involving contractors or normal production activity needs additional coordination because unfamiliarity and simultaneous work can create hazards.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: Maintenance risk depends on equipment, energy sources, degradation, isolation, access, competence, contractors, environment and task planning.

rows.source: HSE work-equipment maintenance and inspection safety
rows.verified: HSE maintenance evidence is equipment-, task-, energy-, worker-, workplace- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
